subject: Clarifying dataflow, subprocessors, and output ownership in DPA for BrightHarbor
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA questions on model updates & subprocessors

Grace —

Thanks for the draft DPA. A couple of quick asks from our security and procurement teams before we route this for signature:

1) We need an explicit commitment that BrightHarbor data will not be used to improve or retrain any models (no model improvement / no-training). Can you confirm the exact contract wording you propose and whether Redwood has an operational proof path for this?

2) We need a current subprocessor inventory and a cadence — procurement requires notification 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor that might process EU customer data.

3) Related to (1): we also need clarity on prompt/response ownership — we own our prompts and the generated responses (output), and we require exportability of any associated telemetry on request.

If you can send redlines or your recommended language and any evidence links, we can return with a short list of exceptions.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security & Privacy, BrightHarbor
liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com>
Cc: procurement@brightharbor.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA questions on model updates & subprocessors

Liam — thanks for the clear list. High level: we can commit contractually to not using BrightHarbor production interaction data to improve our upstream model weights (we call this a model-improvement-exclusion). Operationally we back that up with: a) segregated ingestion pipelines, b) a logging toggle that marks tenant traffic as nonimprovable, and c) quarterly attestations from our Ops team for customers that require audit evidence.

I attached a redlined DPA draft with suggested language and a current subprocessor inventory. Key points in the draft:
- "No model improvement": Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve base models.
- "Output entitlement": Customer retains rights to prompts and generated outputs; Redwood retains service telemetry for billing/ops but will provide exports upon request as described in Section 7.
- "Subprocessor notification": Redwood provides a current inventory and will notify Customer 30 days prior to adding subprocessors that would process Customer data in the EU.

Next steps: I want to loop Kimberley (cc'd) and David in for any tighter legal/ops language you need. If those terms look broadly acceptable, we can move to DocuSign and attach our attestation pack (ops proof links).

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft.docx; subprocessor_inventory_202705.pdf

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightharbor.com>, procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: 2027-05-17T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA questions on model updates & subprocessors

Grace — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few tactical clarifications after a brief review with legal:

- The phrase "will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve base models" is close but procurement wants to include "including via derived features, embeddings, prompts, or evaluation datasets" to avoid ambiguous indirect use.

- For telemetry/exportability: procurement wants a defined SLA for exports (e.g., 14 business days) and a sample schema of what telemetry fields are retained. Can you provide the schema or a sample CSV?

- Subprocessors: the inventory PDF looks good. Two asks: (a) can Redwood commit to an EU-only processing fallback for BrightHarbor traffic (i.e., route to EU-only pools) and (b) confirm whether any subprocessors are located in the US and process EU customer data today.

If Kimberley or David can weigh in on the suggested wording and operational SLAs that would help us close.

Thanks,
Liam

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-17T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA questions on model updates & subprocessors

Hi Liam — looping in David for operational confirmation and adding proposed contract language below that tries to capture your three bullets. Happy to iterate quickly.

Proposed contract snippets (suggested insertion to Section 4 - Use of Customer Content):
1) "Model Improvement Exclusion": "Provider shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, augment, evaluate, or otherwise improve any machine learning models or model weights, whether directly or indirectly (including via derived features, embeddings, prompts, or evaluation datasets)."

2) "Exportability & Telemetry": "Provider will retain service telemetry necessary for billing and platform stability. Upon Customer request, Provider will export retained telemetry related to Customer interactions within 14 business days in a machine-readable format (CSV/JSON). A sample telemetry schema is available at [drive link]; Provider's retention and minimal fields include: request_id, timestamp, model_version, region, token_count, and response_status. Sensitive prompt text is flagged and can be redacted at Customer's request prior to export."

3) "Subprocessor & Residency Controls": "Provider maintains an inventory of subprocessors and will notify Customer at least 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessor expected to process Customer Content in the EU. Provider will offer an EU-only routing configuration for Customer traffic where feasible; any exceptions will be disclosed in the subprocessor inventory. Current subprocessors that process EU customer data are listed in the attached inventory; none of the listed subprocessors perform model training on Customer Content."

Operational note from Ops (David): please confirm routing/residency feasibility and whether we can commit to EU-only pools for BrightHarbor under a Dedicated routing flag.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Legal, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.ai <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightharbor.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-18T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA questions on model updates & subprocessors

Liam / Kimberley / Grace — operational confirmation:

- EU-only routing: yes, we can enable an EU-only processing route for BrightHarbor traffic. That will be a configuration toggle on the customer's profile that pins inference requests to our EU regions and associated GPU pools. We'll include this as an option in the SOW; if BrightHarbor requires Dedicated capacity we can guarantee onshore processing in EU data centers.

- Subprocessors in the US: we have analytics and alerting vendors in the US that receive aggregated telemetry for platform health, but those vendors do not receive unredacted Customer Content and are contractually prohibited from using data for model training. We'll call this out explicitly in the inventory PDF and the DPA annex.

- Telemetry schema & SLA: attached is a sample CSV schema (link in Drive); 14-business-day export turnaround is feasible for this deal tier. For customers that need faster compliance delivery we can add an expedited support SLA in the procurement addendum.

If BrightHarbor is comfortable with Kimberley's proposed language and the operational commitments above, Grace — please propose a DocuSign step and we'll prepare the attestation pack (quarterly Ops attestation + runbook).

Thanks,
David Kim
VP, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
